quotes.text: SharePoint lists were never designed to function as centralized business databases. They were meant for content tracking, not relationship enforcement or role based security

quotes.text: Ask your team who owns the data in this app. If the answer is a person, you're in SharePoint land. If the answer is a role, you're thinking data Verse.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Offers a simple diagnostic question for choosing the right data platform.

quotes.text: If the data outlives the project, it belongs in data verse, it's not sentimentality, it's architecture.

takeaways: SharePoint lists are fine for prototypes and static reference data but break down with relationships, delegation limits, view thresholds and fragmented ownership.
Dataverse brings relational integrity, environment separation, role-based and field-level security, and Purview DLP integration that make governance part of the platform.
Choose by user volume, data sensitivity, relational complexity and lifecycle: if the data outlives the project or is owned by a role, build it in Dataverse.
hook: Starting every Power App on SharePoint lists feels free, but it quietly creates sprawl, broken lookups and audit headaches. This episode helps Power Platform makers and IT decision-makers see when lists stop scaling and why Dataverse is the governed, often cheaper foundation for business-critical apps.
